paper.title: Adaptive Incentive Design in Dynamic Principal-Agent Problem via Kernelized Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic principal-agent contract design with stochastic agent utility (kernelized bandit with heteroscedastic noise)
unmapped: Kernel is the arcsin / neural-network (erf) kernel of Williams (1998), not among the vocabulary families
Contract space X=[0,1]^m with m the number of outcomes (dimension d=m)
Reward is the principal's utility (v-x)_i with outcome i drawn from a production function induced by a strategic agent's best response under random utility perturbation (hidden action / moral hazard)
Noise variance function lies in an RKHS of a kernel kappa^v with norm bound B_v known to the learner; variance bounded by chi_u known to the learner
Sample-variance noise eta(x_t) is rho_eta(x_t)-sub-Gaussian with known rho_eta
Each round the learner samples the chosen contract ell times (repeated sampling)
Agent has a finite action set
settings.definition_quote: the principal posts a contract $x_t \in \mathcal{X}:= [0,1]^m$ ... $\tilde{y}_t= \tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}(x_t) + \tilde{\varepsilon}(x_t)$, where $\tilde{\varepsilon}(x_t)$ is assumed to be a zero-mean heteroscedastic noise ... $\Tilde{R}_T= T\Tilde{U}^{\mathrm{P}*} - \sum_{t=1}^T \Tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}(x_t)$

algorithms.name: Heteroscedastic GP-UCB (with Neural Network / arcsin kernel)

conditions: Utility in RKHS of arcsin NN kernel with ||U^PA||_{H_k} <= B
Noise variance function in RKHS of kappa^v with norm <= B_v (Assumption 4.2)
Sample-variance noise rho_eta(x)-sub-Gaussian with known rho_eta, independent in time (Assumption 4.3)
tuning: beta_t as in eq. (beta_t) with confidence delta

source.label: main_theorem
source.quote: Consider $\tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}} \in \mathcal{H}_k$ with bounded RKHS-norm (i.e., $\|\tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}\|_{\mathcal{H}_k} \le B$) and sampling model in \eqref{feedback_eq} with unknown variance ... Setting $\lambda=1$ in \eqref{beta_t}, the cumulative regret $\Tilde{R}_T$ defined in \eqref{reg_final} is bounded as $\mathbb{P}\left[\Tilde{R}_T \leq \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{T}(\log T)^{m+1}\right)\right] \geq 1 - \delta$

results.notes: Paper's m (contract dimension / number of outcomes) mapped to d. Regret is measured on the smoothed expected utility; rounds count contract postings, each with ell samples. Horizon labelled anytime since the algorithm loop and beta_t do not use T, but this is not stated explicitly. Proof is asymptotic (T -> infinity) and relies on an information-gain bound derived from Proposition 4.4.
